legalRules.title: Retention duty for records
legalRules.proposition: An operator within Article 2 must retain each record for 7 days, subject to Article 3.
applicabilityConditions: The operator offers the notice service to the public (not private household use)
qualifiers: Subject to exception for temporary test records
exceptions: The retention duty does not apply to a temporary test record

legalRules.title: Keep notice text with receipt timestamp
legalRules.proposition: Keep the notice text with its receipt timestamp.
applicabilityConditions: The operator offers the notice service to the public (not private household use)
Applies to records that must be retained under the 7-day retention duty
qualifiers: The receipt timestamp begins the retention period
A receipt timestamp is recorded when the notice is received, not when it is drafted
exceptions: Does not apply to temporary test records

legalRules.title: Preserve notice text without removing limiting language
legalRules.proposition: Preserve the notice text without removing its limiting language.
applicabilityConditions: The operator offers the notice service to the public (not private household use)
Applies to records that must be retained under the 7-day retention duty
exceptions: Does not apply to temporary test records

legalRules.title: Appoint person to attend annual public information session
legalRules.proposition: The operator must appoint a person to attend the annual public information session in person.
applicabilityConditions: The operator offers the notice service to the public (not private household use)
qualifiers: Attendance is recorded in the session register maintained by the organizer

coverage.nonAssessableReason: This duty requires appointing a person and ensuring in-person attendance at an external annual session. A repository cannot establish appointment records, physical attendance, or the existence of session registers maintained by external organizers.

engineeringRules.legalIntent: Ensure that operators retain notice records (stored notice text with receipt timestamp) for 7 days from receipt, excluding temporary test records.
engineeringRules.applicabilityGuidance: Applies to systems that store notices for operators offering the notice service to the public. Does not apply to private household use or temporary test records.

criteria.statement: Each non-temporary-test record must be retained for at least 7 days from its receipt timestamp.
Each retained record must include both the notice text and its receipt timestamp.
The receipt timestamp must reflect when the notice was received, not when it was drafted.

investigationGoals: Identify where notice records are stored
Confirm that notice text and timestamp are stored together
Check for exclusion of temporary test records from retention requirements
edgeStrategies: Follow data flow from notice receipt to storage
patterns: Scheduled cleanup jobs that respect retention period
requiredEvidence: Storage schema showing notice text field and receipt timestamp field together
Code that records receipt timestamp at time of notice receipt (not draft creation)
Evidence that temporary test records are excluded from retention requirements
supportingEvidence: Automated cleanup jobs scheduled based on receipt timestamp + 7 days
Unit tests verifying retention period enforcement
negativeEvidence: Records deleted before 7 days elapse (except temporary test records)
Receipt timestamp recorded at draft time rather than receipt time
Notice text stored without accompanying timestamp
No distinction between temporary test records and regular records
unresolvedConditions: Definition of 'temporary test record' must be determined from system context

engineeringRules.legalIntent: Ensure that the notice text is preserved in its original form without removal of limiting language or qualifiers.
engineeringRules.applicabilityGuidance: Applies to all stored notice records subject to the retention duty. Does not apply to temporary test records.

criteria.statement: Notice text must be preserved without removing limiting language, qualifiers, or conditional phrases.
No text modification or sanitization that removes limiting language is permitted during storage or retrieval.

investigationGoals: Identify notice text storage and retrieval mechanisms
Check for text processing, sanitization, or modification logic
Verify that original notice content is preserved intact
Confirm no removal of limiting language during storage lifecycle
edgeStrategies: Follow data flow from notice receipt through storage to retrieval
Trace text processing or transformation logic
patterns: Direct storage of original notice text without modification
Version control or audit trail showing no text removal
requiredEvidence: Storage implementation that preserves original notice text verbatim
Absence of text sanitization or limiting-language removal in storage path
Code review showing no stripping of qualifiers or conditional phrases
supportingEvidence: Unit tests verifying text integrity preservation
Documentation stating that original notice text is stored unmodified
Audit logs showing notice text remains unchanged
negativeEvidence: Text processing that removes phrases like 'subject to', 'provided that', 'except', 'unless', or similar limiting language
Sanitization routines that strip conditional clauses
Evidence of notice text modification between receipt and storage
unresolvedConditions: Specific examples of 'limiting language' must be identified from actual notice content
